meta.title: 765-kV transmission lines, 10 days of posts
meta.subject: the 765-kilovolt transmission line build-out in Texas — the PUC and ERCOT extra-high-voltage backbone (Permian Basin reliability plan and statewide 765-kV network), line routing, landowner and eminent-domain objections, cost to ratepayers, and whether the lines serve data centers and industry or everyday reliability
meta.subtitle: Oct 6 to Oct 15, 2026. Each dot is one post with 1K+ views about Texas's 765-kV transmission lines, plus every post repeating an earlier one, in the lane for what it argues. Higher and bigger means more views. White means 90% or more the same words as an earlier post, with a white line back to it. Coloured lines link a post to the post it quoted or replied to. Updated daily.

lanes.label: Lines built for data centers
lanes.description: The 765-kV lines are being driven through private land mainly to serve data centers and big industrial load, not everyday Texans.

lanes.label: ERCOT large-load queue overwhelms planning
lanes.description: Gigawatt-scale load requests are swamping ERCOT's transmission planning, so the grid is the real bottleneck for AI and growth.

lanes.label: Build grid to power growth
lanes.description: Expanding transmission and power capacity is needed to power American industry, AI and jobs, and the buildout should move quickly.

lanes.label: Candidates campaign against 765-kV
lanes.description: Texas candidates and officials use opposition to the 765-kV lines as a campaign and legislative issue to win rural and landowner votes.

lanes.label: Permian plan and oil-gas load
lanes.description: The Permian Basin reliability plan and the West Texas grid are framed around oil-and-gas electrification, congestion and curtailed power, with industry seeking exemptions or benefits.

lanes.label: Landowners vs eminent domain
lanes.description: Residents and landowners are fighting the lines, and the government taking their land by eminent domain, on property-rights grounds.

lanes.label: Pushback
lanes.description: Posts doubting, mocking, fact-checking or arguing against the dominant framings.

posts.name: Sam
posts.text:
The core issue for ERCOT (or any bulk power system) is that the legacy transmission planning process becomes a fundamentally intractable/unverifiable problem for the modern scale of load growth 

You cannot produce firm solutions for service to single point loads exceeding 1GW each if the total quantity of load evaluated would double the size of the system

It’s not that we are arriving at the wrong solutions, it’s that we are asking the wrong questions

posts.name: Milk Road AI
posts.text:
Texas just exposed the real AI bottleneck and it will  make already powered data centers dramatically more valuable.

ERCOT’s large load queue exploded from 63 GW to 474 GW in only 18 months, more than five times Texas’ record peak demand and around 90% of the requests involve data centers. But most of that capacity is not close to operating. Only 9.5 GW has been approved and roughly 4.3 GW is running. The rest includes duplicates, speculative applications and developers requesting power at multiple sites.

Texas has paused new data center approvals while ERCOT audits the queue. The state wants to identify credible, financed projects before forcing customers to fund billions of dollars in grid upgrades for campuses that may never exist. This makes secured power more valuable than available land or announced capacity. A developer can own GPUs and property but still wait five to ten years for transmission lines, substations and grid approval.

Galaxy Digital is one of the clearest beneficiaries. Its Helios campus already has more than 1.6 GW of ERCOT approved and utility-contracted power, placing it far ahead of speculative projects still waiting in the queue. $GLXY has already delivered 133 MW of critical IT capacity to CoreWeave under a 15 year lease. CoreWeave has committed to 526 MW across the first three phases, which Galaxy expects to produce more than $1 billion in average annual revenue.The company also has an additional 830 MW of approved Helios capacity available for future tenants and a Texas development pipeline exceeding 5.7 GW.

Applied Digital, TeraWulf and Cipher Mining could benefit for similar reasons. Their former crypto infrastructure provides land, grid relationships and high-power facilities that can be converted into AI campuses faster than completely new developments. The second group of winners sells the equipment needed to solve the shortage. GE Vernova and Siemens Energy supply generation equipment, while Eaton, Schneider Electric, Hubbell and Quanta Services benefit from spending on switchgear, transformers, substations and transmission. Tesla and other storage providers benefit as batteries help stabilize volatile AI workloads.

posts.name: White House Press Pool Reports
posts.text:
President Trump Is Putting American Industry, Jobs, and Paychecks Back on the Map

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

President Donald J. Trump is delivering on his promise to the American worker: build it here, power it here, and put paychecks back in the communities Washington left behind. In a matter of weeks, President Trump has locked in a run of steel, nuclear, gas, shipbuilding, and medical manufacturing commitments that will hire American workers and strengthen American security.
• President Trump announced that Mesabi Metallics will build a $15 billion steel complex in Iowa the largest steel plant ever built in the United States. Fed by American iron ore and driven by the Trump Administration’s steel tariffs, the fully integrated mine-to-mill complex will create 1,750 new, permanent jobs, support up to 6,000 construction jobs, and generate an estimated $95 billion in economic output.

• President Trump and Anduril announced Arsenal-2, the biggest new American shipyard push since World War II, now moving forward in Maryland. The yard will produce critical Virginia-class components and large assemblies, create about 3,100 direct jobs, and support more than 11,000 indirect jobs. Anduril is investing $3.7 billion in private capital; the Navy is putting up to $2.9 billion behind it as part of the Trump Administration’s push to reshore America’s defense industrial base.

• President Trump unveiled a South Korean energy investment package of up to $200 billion in the United States. The package includes as much as $120 billion to build eight large-scale nuclear plants, $54 billion tied to the Alaska LNG pipeline, and $22.3 billion for a six-gigawatt natural gas power facility in Texas.

• Vice President Vance announced that the Department of Energy will invest $150 million to advance a major new transmission line in Alaska. The project includes 223 miles linking the Beluga power station on the southern coast with Healy in the Interior, a corridor serving ports and nearly three-quarters of the state’s population.

• Becton Dickinson announced a $19 billion U.S. investment under a landmark partnership with the Trump Administration, including $3 billion to expand American manufacturing. BD will produce 100% of the needles it sells in America with American-made steel and expand domestic output of essential products.

• AstraZeneca announced a $1 billion investment in Massachusetts under the $50 billion investment commitment it made in its Most Favored Nation agreement with the Trump Administration. The company is expanding its domestic research and manufacturing operation and growing its domestic workforce.

October 8th, 2026.

posts.name: Soluna
posts.text:
In 2024, the West zone in #ERCOT experienced a total curtailment of 5.3 TWh of renewable energy 

That's power already generated, then thrown away because the grid couldn't move it.

Building compute at the source changes the math. Producers earn revenue on power they'd otherwise lose. AI workloads get power faster. Ratepayers carry less of the cost of new transmission.

This isn't a sustainability story. It's grid economics.

It's the model behind Project Dorothy, our data center co-located with a 150 MW wind farm in West Texas.

$SLNH
